purpose: A space between selectors can reach descendants at any depth. The > sign narrows the relationship to a direct child: an element immediately inside the selected parent.
inputsOrValues: In .shelf > p, .shelf selects the parent and p selects its direct paragraph children. The + sign selects the immediately following sibling with the same parent; ~ allows any following matching sibling. These signs describe relationships, not text characters to search for.

purpose: Square brackets can select elements using an HTML attribute. [data-tags="urgent"] requires the whole value to equal urgent. [data-tags~="urgent"] instead looks for urgent as one word in a space-separated list.
inputsOrValues: The custom data-tags attribute stores text for this example; it does not itself change styling. ~= matches a complete list token, so urgently is not urgent. ^= tests whether the value begins with the supplied text; it does not require a whole token. Quoted values belong inside the square brackets.

purpose: nth-child() counts element siblings, starting at one. p:nth-child(2) matches a paragraph only when it is the second element child. nth-of-type() counts only siblings with the same element type.
inputsOrValues: In p:nth-of-type(2), the p before the colon selects paragraphs and the 2 inside parentheses requests the second paragraph among its siblings. Text nodes do not count as element positions. odd and even select alternating positions. This is a CSS selector function, not a JavaScript call; it returns matching elements conceptually, not a value your program receives.

purpose: :where() groups selector alternatives while contributing zero specificity, including its arguments. :is() can match the same elements but takes the specificity of its most specific argument. Here all rules are normal author rules in one layer.
inputsOrValues: The selector inside parentheses decides which elements match. :where(#notice) can match that ID without giving the rule ID-level specificity. The later p rule wins here. Replacing where with is gives the matching rule ID-level specificity, which outranks a type selector in this isolated comparison. Layers and importance are separate earlier cascade decisions.

purpose: inherit takes a property’s computed value from the parent, even for a property that normally does not inherit. initial uses the property’s specified initial value. unset chooses inheritance for inherited properties and the initial value for other properties.

In this page, color: unset takes teal from the parent, while padding-left: unset becomes its initial 0px. initial is not a promise to restore a browser’s complete default stylesheet. These keywords affect the named property, not every style on the element.

purpose: calc() combines compatible quantities into a CSS value. In width: calc(100% - 40px), the percentage uses the containing block’s width and 40px is subtracted from that length. The result is a CSS length, not a JavaScript number.

purpose: A unitless line-height is a multiplier. Descendants inherit the multiplier and apply it to their own font size. This helps a larger child keep proportional line spacing rather than inheriting one fixed pixel height.

If the parent instead specifies30px, that fixed length is inherited, so the larger child also has30px line height. Line height controls line boxes; it is not the visible ink height of every character.
